quality_guards: Platform risk depends on geometry, curvature, rolling stock, passenger flow, accessibility needs, dispatch method and operating conditions.
Station and platform guidance is location-, train-, passenger-, dispatch- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level incident probability.
Trespass risk depends on fencing, access points, surrounding land use, human behaviour, surveillance, response and local network conditions.
Railway criminal-behaviour evidence is route-, location-, access-, population- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level casualty probability.
Man-overboard risk depends on vessel type, deck layout, sea state, weather, task, clothing, flotation, crew competence and recovery resources.
Recovery evidence is vessel-, equipment-, crew-, environmental- and casualty-specific and is not an exact parcel-level drowning probability.
Beacon effectiveness depends on registration data, coding, installation, maintenance, battery condition, satellite visibility and rescue coordination.
Maritime distress-radio evidence is vessel-, equipment-, registration-, location- and incident-specific and is not an exact parcel-level rescue probability.
Rabies risk depends on country, animal species, exposure type, wound site, timing, vaccination history and access to treatment.
Rabies guidance is exposure-, traveller-, animal-, treatment- and timing-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.
Lyme risk depends on tick species, infection status, attachment duration, habitat, season, clothing, removal timing and individual factors.
Tick and Lyme evidence is habitat-, exposure-, symptom-, diagnostic- and person-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.
A Yellow Card report is a safety signal whose interpretation depends on clinical history, exposure, timing, product use and other possible causes.
Yellow Card evidence is report-, patient-, product-, exposure- and time-specific and does not establish an exact parcel-level risk probability.
Restraint suitability depends on the child’s age, height, weight, seat, vehicle, restraint design, installation and permitted exception.
Child-restraint evidence is child-, vehicle-, seat-, journey- and installation-specific and is not an exact parcel-level injury probability.
Towing risk depends on vehicle and trailer compatibility, load distribution, coupling, tyres, brakes, speed, wind, road and driver competence.
Towing evidence is combination-, load-, route-, weather-, maintenance- and driver-specific and is not an exact parcel-level collision probability.
Load movement risk depends on mass, centre of gravity, friction, vehicle body, restraint rating, gaps, route, braking and unloading method.
Load-securing evidence is vehicle-, load-, restraint-, route-, handling- and condition-specific and is not an exact parcel-level road-casualty probability.
Official-source context is not converted into an exact parcel-level probability.
